title: Encode and Decode Strings
kidExplanation: Pack many postcards into one suitcase string, then unpack them later without mixing — even if a postcard contains commas or weird marks.
plainProblem: Design encode/decode for a list of strings so encode(decode(strs)) restores the original list.

examples.explanation: Delimiters inside strings must not break parsing.

thinkingSteps.title: Naive delimiter
thinkingSteps.body: Joining with commas fails if a string contains commas.

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: Store length prefixes: 4#lint4#code … so you always know how many characters to read.

thinkingSteps.title: Better idea
thinkingSteps.body: Encode walks strings appending len + '#' + body. Decode reads numbers until '#', then slices.

thinkingSteps.title: Why interviewers like it
thinkingSteps.body: Shows careful parsing and edge-case thinking.

pattern.name: Hash set / hash map for seen items
pattern.whenToSpot: You need fast lookups of values you already saw.

solutions.python:
# Encode and Decode Strings — interview-friendly solution from NeetCode 150 repo
# Comments explain the idea; logic is unchanged.

class Codec:
    def encode(self, strs: List[str]) -> str:
        encoded = ""
        for s in strs:
            encoded += str(len(s)) + "#" + s
        return encoded

    def decode(self, s: str) -> List[str]:
        decoded = []
        i = 0
        while i < len(s):
            delimiter_pos = s.find("#", i)
            size = int(s[i:delimiter_pos])
            start_pos = delimiter_pos + 1
            end_pos = start_pos + size
            decoded.append(s[start_pos:end_pos])
            i = end_pos
        return decoded

complexity.timeReason: We read and write each character a constant number of times.
complexity.spaceReason: The encoded string and decoded list hold all character data.
